harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 (Alpine), keeping 7 compressed rotations via copytruncate so the application keeps writing to the same path/inode after rotation. Installed logrotate, added /etc/logrotate.d/inventory, enabled+started crond (was stopped) so /etc/periodic/daily actually fires. Verified rotation behavior with a forced run, then restarted node1 and confirmed persistence and recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine 3.23, no logrotate installed, crond stopped, /var/log/inventory/app.log present with static content, no running app process
Installed logrotate (and logrotate-openrc) via apk, providing /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate hook that reads /etc/logrotate.d/
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory: daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Enabled and started crond (rc-update add crond default; rc-service crond start) so daily periodic jobs actually run
Validated config with logrotate -d (dry run) showing correct daily/7-rotation pattern

Forced rotation with logrotate -f, confirmed compressed archive app.log-20260929.gz created, app.log inode unchanged (copytruncate), and new writes appended successfully to the same path before and after rotation
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, crond status, logrotate config, app.log/rotated file contents
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id (a7ca5ddf-bd48-45e9-9171-2bddb38f1a6d -> 71fabf0a-7342-4471-8abe-9ec61b75f1a9) and low uptime proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart verified crond auto-started and is enabled in default runlevel, logrotate config intact, rotated .gz archive intact, and app.log still writable (wrote and read back a post-reboot line)

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
evidence.summary: logrotate -d dry-run shows pattern: /var/log/inventory/app.log after 1 days, 7 rotations

evidence.requirement: Rotation actually works and produces a compressed archive
evidence.summary: Forced logrotate run created app.log-20260929.gz; zcat confirms it holds the pre-rotation log content

evidence.requirement: Application continues writing after rotation (no restart/signal needed)
evidence.summary: copytruncate config used; inode of app.log unchanged before/after rotation (65543), and a write immediately after rotation succeeded and landed in the fresh app.log

evidence.requirement: Rotation is scheduled to run automatically (daily cron)
evidence.summary: crond enabled+started; /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate script (installed by apk package) invokes logrotate against /etc/logrotate.conf which includes /etc/logrotate.d/
boot_id a7ca5ddf..., crond started, logrotate config and rotated file present
Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id 71fabf0a-7342-4471-8abe-9ec61b75f1a9 (different from baseline a7ca5ddf...) with uptime 17s

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services/config/data
evidence.summary: crond auto-started and enabled at boot, logrotate config intact, rotated .gz intact, and app.log writable post-reboot
